run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/checkout since 2026-11-17T04:12:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The warning is backed by real, sustained checkout request errors: the checkout PlaceOrder span series shows 117.9 error spans versus 518.9 unset spans over the 10 minutes to 2026-11-17T04:47:17Z (about 18.5%, consistent with the alert's 0.19999999999999998), and the 5-minute error increase rises from 0 at 04:12:23Z to about 140 per 5 min by 04:22:23Z and stays between roughly 108 and 155 per 5 min through 04:51:23Z. The failing path is visible in whole traces: checkout PlaceOrder calls prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, whose HTTP POST client span is the only erroring span, and that POST's only visible child is the shipping server span /get-quote lasting 38 to 469 microseconds, which never issues its own child POST quote; checkout then returns gRPC 13 with 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400'. The failing orders carry no line items: 4 of 4 sampled failing traces contain no ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and no CurrencyService/Convert spans, and in the 10-minute window shipping /get-quote (631.6) exceeds quote POST /getquote (518.9) by about 113, matching the 117.9 failed quote POSTs, so those quotes were rejected inside shipping before quote was called. The email service is not the failing dependency despite the message wording: in successful traces the email call is a separate HTTP POST whose POST /send_order_confirmation returned http.status_code 200, and email exposes no error-status series. checkout, email, shipping and cart pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts, their Services/Endpoints map each name to its own pod, cart AddItem/GetCart show 0 error increase, valkey memory peaked at 2813664 bytes, and no shipping or email fault flag exists in flagd-config (all defined fault flags are off). Unresolved: why about 18.5% of PlaceOrder attempts arrive with an empty cart (load-session behaviour versus an application defect) and the exact input or status that makes shipping answer HTTP 400; request bodies, the reply status tag and shipping's log line for the rejected calls are not observable, so those remain hypotheses and no single Kubernetes object is named as root cause.

claims.text: checkout's error signal starts at the alert anchor and is sustained: the 5-min increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",span_name="oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} is 0 at 04:12:23Z, then 4.11, 13.9, 70, 127.8 and 140 by 04:22:23Z, and stays between about 107.8 and 154.9 through 04:51:23Z, while the same span's STATUS_CODE_UNSET increase stays around 453 to 925 per 5 min.

Over the 10 minutes to 2026-11-17T04:47:17Z, checkout PlaceOrder spans were 117.894 error versus 518.947 unset (about 18.5% error share), and checkout's client span 'HTTP POST' was 117.894 error versus 1556.842 unset.

The failing checkout spans record the exact diagnostic text 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400' in otel.status_description and exception.message, with status tags error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=13; the same text appears in frontend as grpc.error_message on grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder.

In trace fabf30c40bb674e79e93dd78836bb231 the only erroring checkout span is 'HTTP POST' (span_id 2f69d09d57973cd9, parent prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart span_id 4e53d77d5e11686f), and its only visible child is shipping's server span '/get-quote' (span_id a170b05e15f5aeba, 469 microseconds); the trace contains no email-service span.

In trace c7625da06fae49e86716ba65e8fc52fb the erroring checkout 'HTTP POST' (span_id e572309e8165581d, 678 microseconds) has as its only child shipping's '/get-quote' (span_id 9a387acfd928f271, 38 microseconds); checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart in that trace returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and there are no ProductCatalogService/GetProduct or CurrencyService/Convert spans.

Across 4 sampled failing checkout traces (754892b63555b89873783ef648997978, c7625da06fae49e86716ba65e8fc52fb, adb3c50d1d124cff7b898569d2f8feba, a8d4c1ce41e831df717b2bb1d32b998c) each trace shows 1 error checkout 'HTTP POST' plus 1 shipping '/get-quote' of 38 to 51 microseconds, and 0 rows of oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, 0 rows of CurrencyService/Convert and 0 rows of quote-service spans.

In successful trace 8e42cf2d98d4fb8a102ab6a2cd3b8747 the shipping quote is a 'HTTP POST' (span_id 2d858b9b5812c20b) whose child shipping '/get-quote' (span_id 93833ae13f5ef61b) has its own child quote 'POST /getquote', and the separate email 'HTTP POST' (span_id da2d9b2670e0b8e2) has child email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' with http.status_code 200.

Over the 10 minutes to 04:47:17Z shipping '/get-quote' spans were 631.579 while quote 'POST /getquote' spans were 518.947 (difference about 112.6, matching the 117.894 failed quote POSTs), and email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' was 514.737, so the rejected quote requests never reached the quote service.

In the same 10-minute window checkout's own spans are PlaceOrder 636.842 (117.894 error plus 518.947 unset), prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart 636.842 and GetCart 636.842, but oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct is only 842.105 and CurrencyService/Convert 1361.053, so product lookups correspond to roughly 1.6 per successful order and do not cover the 117.9 failing orders.

Error-status span series were returned only for checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and a small recommendation background (1.11 per 5 min) at 04:47:17Z; no error-status series was returned for shipping, email, cart, quote, currency, product-catalog or payment, so their error counts are unknown rather than zero.

Email's span metrics contain only STATUS_CODE_UNSET series: 'POST /send_order_confirmation' and 'send_email' at about 181 to 297 per 5 min and 'sinatra.render_template' at about 318 to 596 per 5 min through 04:51:23Z; no error-status email series exists.

The cart path shows no failures: frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' 1960 with 0 error increase and 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' 2954.737 with 0 error increase over 10 min, and checkout-side 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' returns rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in every sampled trace, failing and successful alike.

checkout, email and shipping pods were Running and ready with 0 restarts, started 2026-11-17T04:02:14-04:02:15Z (checkout-5dccddf8bb-vh65b, email-59f69bc6cf-7wqqk, shipping-75d58f5d84-kgmz9), and their Services/Endpoints map each name to its own pod (shipping 8080 to shipping-75d58f5d84-kgmz9 100.96.3.37; email 8080 to email-59f69bc6cf-7wqqk 100.96.3.192).

checkout's Deployment environment sets EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080 and SHIPPING_ADDR=http://shipping:8080 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout), and email's Deployment uses image 2.1.3-email with EMAIL_PORT=8080, so no address cross-wiring is visible in the current objects.

The flagd-config ConfigMap defines no shipping or email failure flag, and every fault flag it does define is at variant 'off' (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure), with only loadGeneratorFloodHomepage at defaultVariant '100'.

The only otel-demo events inside the window concern the load-generator Deployment: at 04:36:29-04:36:30Z 'Scaled up replica set load-generator-7d5756fbd9 from 0 to 1', pod load-generator-7d5756fbd9-zzj4z Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started, and old replica set load-generator-c7cbc4c99 scaled to 0 with pod load-generator-c7cbc4c99-xlnk2 killed; no events exist for checkout, shipping, email or cart pods.

The cart and valkey-cart pods (cart-755465879b-j4pxv, valkey-cart-58df56c79c-kt7dp) are Running and ready with 0 restarts since 04:02:14-15Z, and valkey's memory used peaked at 2813664 bytes inside the window.

The shipping container log in 04:10-04:30Z contains success-path lines ('Requesting quote', 'Sending Quote', 'Tracking ID Created'), and checkout's container log shows the success path ('payment went through', 'order placed', 'order confirmation email sent to ...') including for orders placed during the alert window.

This Prometheus exposes no HTTP or RPC server metric: http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_server_* returned nothing, and the only application-level metrics present are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket.

Most likely mechanism: checkout's prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart sends the quote POST with no line items (no GetProduct or Convert work happens for those orders) and the shipping service answers HTTP 400 immediately in 38 to 51 microseconds without calling quote; checkout surfaces that 400 as gRPC 13 'shipping quote failure: ...expected 200, got 400', which becomes the frontend 500 and the checkout error-rate alert. Not verified: the request body and the shipping reply's status tag are not visible in the span projection and shipping logs contain no line for the rejected calls.

Why about 18.5% of PlaceOrder attempts present an empty cart: the load-generator checkout scenarios ('user_checkout_single' and 'user_checkout_multi') can reach /api/checkout for a session whose cart is already empty, for example after a previous successful order emptied it, rather than because the cart service lost data, since cart AddItem/GetCart show 0 error increase, checkout-side GetCart returns status 0, and cart plus valkey pods are healthy. Not verified: per-session cart contents and the load-generator task sequence are not observable.

The email service returning HTTP 400 is not the failing dependency despite checkout's 'failed POST to email service' wording: in the failing traces the erroring client span's only child is shipping '/get-quote', email has no error-status span series, and in successful traces the email confirmation call returned http.status_code 200.

No flagd fault-injection setting matches this failure path: the ConfigMap has no shipping or email failure flag, and all fault flags it defines (adFailure, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems) are at variant 'off'.

The 04:36:29Z load-generator Deployment rollout (new replica set load-generator-7d5756fbd9, old pod killed) is not the trigger of this alert: checkout's error increase is already about 140 per 5 min at 04:22:23Z, more than 14 minutes before that rollout, and remains elevated at 04:51:23Z.

Pod-level damage in checkout, email, shipping or cart is not the cause: all four pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 since 04:02Z, no pod event in the window shows Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Unhealthy or Failed, and the failing trace shows a fast orderly HTTP response rather than a crash or connection refusal.

checkout's status description names the email service while the observed failing call targets shipping, so the service name inside that message cannot be used to identify the failing dependency; the trace topology is the stronger evidence and the message is inexact or mislabelled in this code path.

shipping's '/get-quote' server spans carry no status tags (status_state not_recorded) and shipping has no error-status metric series, yet the aggregate shows about 113 of its 631.6 quote requests in 10 min never reached quote while the matching checkout client span is marked error, so the absence of shipping-side error signals does not mean those replies succeeded.

Advice for the owning team: verify shipping /get-quote behaviour for a request whose item list is empty (it currently answers HTTP 400 in 38 to 51 microseconds before contacting quote) and decide whether checkout should reject an empty cart before calling shipping instead of turning that 400 into a gRPC INTERNAL error.

Advice: instrument or log the shipping /get-quote 4xx path, or expose the HTTP status tag on checkout's client span, and add an explicit empty-cart log line in checkout, because today neither the pod logs nor the span projection shows the request body or the rejected status, which is what blocks a definitive root cause.

gaps: No Prometheus sample earlier than 2026-11-17T04:12:23Z was returned (the 24h range query with a 600s step produced points only from 04:17:17Z onward), so there is no pre-alert baseline for checkout's error rate; the first in-window sample at 04:12:23Z shows a 5-min increase of 0, but whether the condition predates the alert window is unknown.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate returned no data from list_prometheus_rules, so its expression, 0.2 threshold and evaluation interval are unverified; the alert annotation remains the only statement of the rule.

Request bodies, the URL and http.status_code of the failing checkout HTTP POST to shipping and of shipping's 400 reply are not exposed by the span projection, so 'empty item list' as the reason for the HTTP 400 is a hypothesis, not a verified fact.

shipping's container log in 04:10-04:30Z shows only success-path lines and no line for the rejected /get-quote calls; several log and trace queries returned no rows (email pod log filtered and unfiltered, shipping log filtered for error terms, checkout log filtered for error terms, shipping and email and checkout traces filtered by error tags in later windows, and the metric lookups for http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_server_*), and those empty results are stated limits of this Run, not proof that nothing happened.
Jaeger held traces only up to about 2026-11-17T04:17:02Z and only recent traces, so there is no trace evidence for 04:17-04:52Z, the majority of the alert period.

The load-generator Deployment was rolled out at 04:36:29Z (replica set load-generator-7d5756fbd9 replaced load-generator-c7cbc4c99); the old pod template is gone, so what changed in the load generator (task mix, user count, cart behaviour) is unknown.
No change_history integration is available in this Run, so no deployment, configuration or flag change record can be correlated with the 04:12:23Z onset.
Kubernetes objects were read at query time (about 04:52Z) and cannot prove their state during the incident; secret-backed values could not be read.

The reason about 18.5% of PlaceOrder attempts carry no cart items (client session behaviour versus an application defect in cart retrieval) could not be determined from the spans, metrics or logs available.
next_steps: Check shipping's /get-quote handler contract for zero-item requests and decide whether the 400 is intended; if it is, make checkout reject an empty cart before the quote call and return a non-error status.
Capture one failing request and response pair between checkout and shipping (body plus HTTP status), or enable HTTP status tags on checkout's client span, to confirm the empty-item hypothesis.
Review the load-generator scenario definitions (user_checkout_single, user_checkout_multi) and its 04:36:29Z rollout to see whether checkout iterations run for sessions with an empty cart.
Load the RequestErrorRate alerting rule into the queried Prometheus, or confirm its expression and threshold, so the alert's 0.2 ratio can be tied to the measured checkout PlaceOrder error share.
If a pre-alert baseline is required, retain or extend metric retention beyond the current data start near 04:12Z.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
